title: FAKE-02 discharge summary (NSTEMI, heart failure)

pages.text:
SYNTHETIC / FAKE TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL PATIENT — FOR SOFTWARE DEMONSTRATION ONLY

Lakeview Test General Hospital (FAKE)

Department of Medicine · 200 Sample Avenue, Testville ON

MRN: FAKE-000123

Discharge Summary

  Patient  Rowan Testwood  DOB  21 June 1958

  Admitted  12 October 2026  Discharged  19 October 2026

  Attending  Dr. Ian Sampleton (Cardiology)  Family physician  Dr. Henrietta Fakeham

Diagnoses

1. Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), treated with a drug-eluting stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery on 13 October 2026

2. New heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: LVEF 40% on echocardiogram (14 October 2026)

3. Acute kidney injury after contrast. Creatinine peaked at 162 µmol/L and was back to 104 µmol/L at discharge.

4. Type 2 diabetes, not at target

5. Hypertension

Presentation

Mr. Testwood came to the emergency department with 40 minutes of chest pressure at rest. The ECG showed 1 mm ST depression in V3 to V6. Troponin rose from 48 ng/L to 1,260 ng/L over 3 hours. He had been referred to cardiology clinic on 2 October 2026 with six weeks of exertional chest pressure.

Hospital course

Coronary disease. Angiography on 13 October showed a 90% proximal LAD stenosis, treated with one drug-eluting stent, and a 50% right coronary stenosis managed medically. There were no complications at the radial access site. He has been free of chest pain since the procedure.

Heart failure. The echocardiogram showed anterior hypokinesis with LVEF 40% and no significant valve disease. He received two doses of furosemide 40 mg IV for mild pulmonary congestion; it is not continued. Discharge weight 92.4 kg.

Kidney function. Creatinine rose after contrast and recovered with IV fluids. Metformin was held from 13 to 17 October and restarted at a lower dose. Ramipril was held for 48 hours and restarted at 2.5 mg.

Diabetes. Glucose 8 to 14 mmol/L in hospital. Glyburide was stopped because of hypoglycemia risk and empagliflozin was started for both diabetes and heart failure. HbA1c is pending.

Medications at discharge

  Medication  Dose  Status

  Acetylsalicylic acid  81 mg daily, indefinitely  Continued

  Ticagrelor  90 mg twice daily for 12 months (until October 2027)  NEW

  Atorvastatin  80 mg daily  CHANGED (was 20 mg)

  Metoprolol  25 mg twice daily  NEW

  Ramipril  2.5 mg daily  CHANGED (was 5 mg)

  Empagliflozin  10 mg daily  NEW

  Metformin  500 mg twice daily  CHANGED (was 1000 mg twice daily)

  Nitroglycerin spray  0.4 mg as needed for chest pain  Continued

  Glyburide  —  STOPPED

Follow-up

- Blood tests in 1 week (around 26 October 2026): creatinine, potassium, CBC. Requisition given.

- Family physician visit within 2 weeks: review the blood tests and the HbA1c result, and adjust ramipril if potassium and kidney function allow.

- Cardiology clinic with Dr. Sampleton in 4 weeks.

- Repeat echocardiogram in 3 months to recheck LVEF.

- Referral sent to the cardiac rehabilitation program.

Instructions to the patient

- Do not stop ticagrelor or acetylsalicylic acid without talking to cardiology. Stopping them early can block the stent.

- No driving for 1 week. No heavy lifting (more than 5 kg) with the right arm for 1 week.

- Weigh yourself every morning. Call if your weight goes up more than 2 kg in 3 days.

- For chest pain, use the spray once. If the pain is not gone after 5 minutes, call 911.

Electronically signed: Dr. Ian Sampleton, MD (FAKE), Cardiology · 19 October 2026

cc: Dr. Henrietta Fakeham (family physician)
